mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within 3 months indicates a weakening labor market, which is a precursor to economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in housing starts over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the observed periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 1% over two consecutive months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% within the same month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which is a positive indicator for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (growth < 0.2%), it signals strong demand without significant inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with a decline in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a tightening monetary policy with a slowing economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a robust supply-side expansion, which is a positive indicator for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the observed periods.
